story_text.value:
Anyone else run into this problem?

I built staaake Meets (staaakemeets.com) because we run side tech events around the world. You create an event once and it can be shared to Luma, Meetup and Eventbrite. I connected each platform through their API and it works great. (not the problem)

Then I wanted to add more platforms, like Partiful, and realized some don't have a public API. I started noticing the same problem with other projects too. There are still a lot of big products that don't have an API or even a developer page.

And now with Claude, ChatGPT and AI agents, it feels like this is becoming a bigger problem. If software and agents are going to interact with products directly, they need a way to access them.

So I built staaake Connector (staaakeconnector.com). You connect your backend, choose what you want to make available, and it creates an API and MCP for your product. It can also give you webhooks and an SDK.

I also turned my community into a network where humans, products and agents can find and connect with each other.

It's live now. I'd really like feedback from people building agents or products that need to interact with other software.

Its been a while i used Hackernews, lets see if its still alive!

title.value: Show HN: I built a tool that gives any website an API and MCP

story_text.value:
Hey HN, this daily puzzle game is inspired by an old flash game "trap the cat" I played ~20 years ago. A friend challenged me to make a small game, and I decided to have a stab. I included special tiles to make it a bit more interesting, but honestly the challenge to do it in as few moves as possible each day is what has kept it interesting for me.

If you want to play a bit more, I just added an archive so past days are accessible.

Let me know what you think, and if you have any comments or suggestions I'd love to hear them :)

story_text.value:
I've been working on this for a while now (I made a POC for myself some years ago which I didn't release. But AI helped me a lot to finally complete/polish it).

Inspired by digital forensic toolkits, this library allows a user to take a c-struct definition and use that to serialize an deserialize binary data.

It is a flexible library which features modern c# mechanisms and conventions. I tried to make it easy to use, easy to understand, performant and powerful. You can both use it to parse and use runtime user defined structures as well as use the C# source generator feature to build parsers/serializers at compile time.

I also build and published a WASM version/javascript library which is used to showcase the features of the library (see the binary inspector demo app (https://vvollers.github.io/cstructsharp/inspector/) which you can use to run the library against various files, it includes sample definitions for many file formats). The library is quite usable on its own.

I'm interested to hear your thoughts and if you have any questions feel free to ask.

title.value: Show HN: CStructSharp – C-struct (de)serialization for C# and JavaScript (WASM)

story_text.value:
I'm not a Data Scientist but have been super intrigued with causal inference off late, so I made a Claude skill to simplify the modelling and experimentation process.

You upload your dataset to Claude (Opus) and this skill picks your brain for your domain knowledge about the dataset and comes up with a causal dag that you can iterate through. It then runs the data through a number of classical statistics, ML and newer transformer models to come up with outcomes. And it finally creates a html report to help you understand the results.
